title: Rubric Self-Check
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Capstone Portfolio
Rubrics
Self-Assessment
MicroSim Quality
description: A Chart.js horizontal stacked bar chart of the seven capstone rubric criteria from Chapter 25 (100 points). Self-rating sliders set points earned against points still available, a total appears above the chart, hovering a bar shows what full credit means, and Suggest next focus highlights the criterion with the most points still available; a text box records the learner's reason. The ratings are a self-assessment, not a grade.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Self-assessing a capstone portfolio against its rubric
learningObjectives: The learner will assess a draft portfolio against the seven rubric criteria and justify which criterion to improve first.
prerequisites: A draft portfolio or the chapter's worked portfolio plan

accessibility.notes: Native labeled range inputs with aria-valuetext giving percent and points; the chart canvas has role=img and an aria-label with every criterion's points; the total and the suggestion are aria-live regions; the suggested criterion is marked by a thick outline and a highlighted slider row as well as color

controls.label: One self-rating slider per criterion
controls.purpose: Set points earned for the criterion

controls.label: Suggest next focus
controls.purpose: Highlight the criterion with the most points still available

controls.label: Your reason for improving it first

assumptions: Ratings are the learner's own estimates, not a grade

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Self-assessment against explicit criteria with prioritization and justification
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Rating sliders driving a stacked bar chart, with a suggestion and a written reason
keyQuestions: Which criterion has the most points still available?
Which improvement do other criteria depend on?
commonMisconceptions: The self-rated total predicts the grade
The criterion with the most points available is always the right first fix
An impressive fidelity number earns more credit than an honest limits sentence
assessmentOpportunities: A written reason that uses points and dependency
